source: CoreGuard Quilla Cyber Codex (original educational summaries; cites public frameworks)

entries.title: Android permission hygiene
entries.summary: Dangerous permissions and special access are high-value for spyware.
entries.body: Be skeptical of Accessibility, Notification Listener, Device Admin, and Accessibility-like overlay powers. Location, mic, camera, SMS, and contacts deserve periodic audits. Deny by default; grant temporarily.
entries.defense: Settings → Privacy/Permission manager. After denying, rescan with Nemesis.

entries.title: Sideloading & unknown apps risk
entries.summary: Sideloaded APKs bypass store review — primary malware path.
entries.body: Prefer Play Store or enterprise-managed stores. Disable install-unknown-apps per-source. Verify publisher reputation. Play Protect helps but is not perfect.
entries.defense: Scan after any APK install. Uninstall first if verdict is hostile.

entries.title: Patch & OS update discipline
entries.summary: Unpatched devices keep known exploitable bugs alive.
entries.body: Install OS, Google Play system, and app updates promptly. Check Security patch level monthly. Older devices that stop receiving patches should be replaced or isolated from sensitive work.
entries.defense: Note patch level in your personal security routine alongside Guardian Score.

entries.title: Strong lock screen & biometrics
entries.summary: Device encryption strength follows your lock screen.
entries.body: Use a strong PIN/passphrase; biometrics are convenience layered on that secret. Avoid weak 4-digit PINs for high-risk users. Auto-lock quickly; disable lock-screen sensitive notifications.
entries.defense: Enable lock now; then revisit notification content on the secure lock screen.

entries.title: Hostile network playbook
entries.summary: Public Wi‑Fi elevates MITM and phishing risk.
entries.body: Prefer cellular or known networks for sensitive tasks. Use VPN when required by policy. Certificate warnings are stop signs. DNS filtering blocks known-bad domains but does not encrypt your traffic alone.
entries.defense: Turn on CoreGuard Shield on untrusted Wi‑Fi; keep HTTPS sites and updated apps.

entries.title: Commercial spyware reality check
entries.summary: High-end spyware is rare but severe; hygiene still matters for everyone.
entries.body: Mercenary spyware may abuse zero-days and leave subtle artifacts. Most users face phishing, malicious apps, and account takeover. Evidence-based tools (MVT-style indicators, on-device scans) help triage — they do not prove a clean bill forever.
entries.defense: CoreGuard uses open Amnesty/mvt-style indicator ideas for on-device triage. Treat CLEAN as encouraging, not eternal.

entries.title: Account takeover defenses
entries.summary: Most real-world harm starts with account compromise.
entries.body: Prefer passkeys or app-based MFA over SMS where possible. Watch for SIM-swap risk. Review account login sessions after suspicious events. Never enter passwords on pages reached from unexpected links.
entries.defense: After a SUSPICIOUS/INFECTED scan, rotate critical accounts from a second clean device.
